title: 3 Calgary police officers charged with manslaughter in death of unarmed Blood Tribe man
summary: Three Calgary police officers have been charged with manslaughter two years after an unarmed Blood Tribe man died while in police custody.

image.caption: Jon Wells, 42, died while in police custody in September 2024. On Monday, three Calgary police officers were charged with manslaughter. (Megan Wells/Facebook)

blocks.text: Calgary·Breaking
Three Calgary police officers have been charged with manslaughter two years after an unarmed Blood Tribe man died while in police custody.
Jon Wells died on Sept. 17, 2024, while restrained, wearing spit hood

Jon Wells, 42, died in September 2024 after he was tackled, punched and subjected to other “uses of force” at the hands of officers, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) said at the time.
The incident took place in the lobby of the Carriage House Hotel and Conference Centre on Macleod Trail.
On Monday, three of the responding officers — Constables Filip Poskovic, 39, Roy Braun, 53, and Vincent Washington, 48, — were charged with manslaughter and assault causing bodily harm.
'Presumed innocent'
Defence lawyer Cory Wilson, who represents Poskovic, provided a brief statement to CBC News, saying his client denies the allegations.
“He is presumed innocent and plans to vigorously defend himself at trial,” said Wilson.
Shamsher Kothari, who represents Braun, also provided a written statement, saying his client “vehemently denies the charges laid today.”
“We look forward to his exoneration within the upcoming judicial proceedings,” Kothari wrote.
Defence lawyer Don MacLeod, who represents Washington, said his client "maintains his innocence and intends to mount a vigorous defence."
Handcuffs, spit hood
The officers were charged Monday morning at the ASIRT office and were released on an undertaking. They are due back in court in January.

items: Unarmed man punched, tackled by officers in altercation that ended in his death: police watchdog

blocks.text: Wells died in the early morning hours of Sept. 17, 2024.

On that day, just before 1 a.m., police were called to the Carriage House Hotel after Wells allegedly refused to leave the lobby. On the day of the incident, CPS said in a release that Wells had been “acting erratically” and was “not co-operative.”
Officers used handcuffs, leg restraints and a spit hood on Wells who was face down on the ground. Minutes later, he was declared dead.
A spit hood — or spit mask — is a face covering that is draped over the heads of people who spit or threaten to as a protection for first responders.
Body-worn video footage
About a week after Wells’ death, ASIRT released details of the interaction between Wells and the officers on-scene based on body-worn camera footage.
According to ASIRT, Wells, who was unarmed, stood with his hands in full view when the first officer arrived and ordered him to leave.
The officer ordered Wells to leave the lobby. Wells acted “in a confused fashion,” according to ASIRT. He tried to pick up items off the floor “that were clearly non-existent.”
After about 30 seconds, the officer pointed his stun gun at Wells who put his hands up, asked the officer not to shoot and said he would leave.
'I don't want to die'
As Wells walked slowly to the main door with his hands raised he said to the officer, “I don’t want to die.” The officer ordered Wells to stop talking and continued to point his weapon at him.
Two other officers arrived through the main lobby door. Again, Wells stated that he didn’t want to die.
The first officer holstered his stun gun and tried to grab Wells.
“At no point during the interaction had the male been identified, nor was he ever told he was being detained or under arrest,” said ASIRT in its September 2024 statement.
'Various uses of force'
Wells “resists being grabbed” and was then tackled by a second officer who punched him in the head while both were on the ground.
The two other officers then shot Wells with their stun guns.
The three officers then spent the next three-and-a-half minutes administering “various uses of force” on Wells before restraining him with handcuffs and leg restraints.

items: Family of Blood Tribe man who died in Calgary Police custody calls for public inquiry

blocks.text: By then, Wells was vomiting and bleeding from the mouth. The officers put a spit hood on him as he laid face down on the floor.
EMS and other officers had arrived at this point and about seven minutes after he was handcuffed, paramedics administered a sedative to Wells, who was still face down.
Wells was left face down in handcuffs, leg restraints and the spit mask for another three minutes until someone at the scene noticed he was unresponsive.
Despite efforts by first responders, Wells was declared dead in the hotel lobby.
CPS has not yet responded to a request for information regarding the employment status of the three officers.
